At steady state the first law gives input power = output power + heat dissipated, with the heat never negative, which is the catalogue's own energy_balance relation and its source ("the first law of thermodynamics for a component at steady state"); so a passive stage's efficiency lies from 0 to 1. A quantity of dimension one, written as a number or a fraction (the SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2019, NIST SP 330-2019, the catalogue's citation for every kind: section 2.3.4 and the notes to Table 4, read via search, not in full, 26.09.2026); read 2026-11-03). Note on the span: A definition, not a product class: no passive stage delivers more than it takes in, so a value above 1 is a mistake in the arithmetic or the unit (a percentage written as a bare number), never a better part. It bounds the size of a value; the sign is the unit check's. Named limit: a ratio written under an efficiency name that is not output over input (a heat pump's coefficient of performance, an active stage's gain) is refused above 1; such a ratio has its own name.
